correctness.rationale: After the probability-integral transform, conditional on the observed uniform being above one half, each antithetic pair contributes a Bernoulli exceedance with success probability uniform on \(0,1\); below one half, it contributes one plus such a Bernoulli. Mixing a \(\operatorname{Binomial}(B,p)\) count over uniform \(p\) gives the exact uniform beta-binomial count on \(\{0,\ldots,B\}\). Combining the two halves proves the mass function and CDF. Direct algebra proves the first failing support level and maximal excess. The packaged checker verifies the identities for \(B\le200\) in exact arithmetic.

value.rationale: Antithetic pairing is a standard variance-reduction device, and the primary source specifically warns that it can destroy p-value validity. The theorem resolves a natural canonical case completely: despite dependence and global invalidity, inverse-CDF reflection preserves every testing level up to \(1/2\), while giving an exact first failure and exact worst additive inflation. This separates a practically safe low-level region from the source paper’s more general caution and quantifies precisely what correct null marginals fail to guarantee.
